title: The school that could turn George into a drama king! Insiders reveal why Princess Kate could be looking at north London school where Jude Law and Emma Thompson sent their children
text:
The Princess of Wales has caused febrile speculations about whether she is looking for a school with latest generation drama facilities for the eldest son Prince George.
Recently he toured two elite schools North London, leaving the parents of the bewildered schools why he could be considering the location.
Both schools, Highgate School and University College School in Hampstead, while only 30 miles from the Windsor base of Wales could create a great headache for daily trips through the capital with expected travel times of more than more than more than more than An hour in each sense.
But, after much debate about the school’s doors, parents in highgate say they know why the princess is attracted to Highgate: she has a “world class” drama department and is the school of choice for the children of Famous Thespians like Emma Thompson.
His drama is so impressive that the historical school is also known for feeding children in the prestigious Royal Academy for Dramatic Arts (Rada), the best graduated drama school in the United Kingdom.
Several famous Luvvies have also sent their children to Highgate over the years, including Gwyneth Paltrow and Jude Law.
His alumni include the actor of the children’s star Freddie Highmore, who starred in Johnny Depp in Finding Neverland.
The princess, now in cancer remission, was seen at the Highgate School of £ 10,000 at the right time after she closed for Christmas holidays.
According to reports, Catherine is considering an excellent drama department for her eldest son Prince George

A source told The Mail on Sunday: ‘The family turned around and took a look and, apparently, it is because the school has a quite bright drama department, really world class.
‘Kate spent a lot of time talking to two of the teachers there, including the head of drama, and asked them about the drama curriculum and extracurricular activities and what opportunities could there be to appear in the school plays.
‘One of the reasons why they are attracted to visit Highgate is that the department is known as somewhere that feeds Rada. Highgate has a very strong approach to Shakespeare with a nuanced and intelligent approach to drama.
‘It is where people send their children if they want a higher place than the British school. Apparently, Kate was informed that this school will help George leave, but not pressurized.
His Alma Mater, Marlborough College in Wiltshire, is still understood that it is the preferred option for George, 11, when the Lambrook school leaves in Berkshire in 18 months, but it is said that Kate and her husband Prince William are “thinking outside The box “and continue looking at other options.
If George really has a flash for the dramatic arts, he would mean that he is following in the footsteps of his grandfather, King Charles and Uncle Abuelo Edward.
The king was at the Cambridge Footlights Club in 1967 and acted many times during his years studying at Trinity College.
A devotee fan of Shakespeare, Charles even acted at the Royal Shakespeare Company in Stratford-Upon-Avon in 2016 to celebrate the bard’s legacy 400 years after the day after his death.
